The Media Information Officer of the task force, Lt-Col Aliyu Danja, disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday in Gusau.
Danja said the rescue followed a distress call received by troops of Sector 1 on October 16, 2026, over terrorist activities in Gamji community, Sabuwa Local Government Area, where 27 residents were reportedly abducted.
According to him, the troops immediately mobilised and pursued the terrorists along the Gangare-Kamba axis.
“On contact, troops engaged with superior firepower, forcing the terrorists to abandon their victims and flee in disarray,” he said.
Danja stated that all 27 victims were rescued unharmed, profiled and handed over to community leaders for reunification with their families.
In a separate operation on the same day, troops on a fighting patrol around Kurba village in Kankara Local Government Area encountered terrorists travelling on three motorcycles.
He said the suspects fled upon sighting the troops, abandoning one of the motorcycles.
“The terrorists fled on sighting troops, abandoning one motorcycle,” Danja added.
He said the operations reflected the task force’s continued offensive against terrorist groups and efforts to prevent them from operating freely and threatening communities.
The Theatre Commander of the Joint Task Force North West, Operation Fansan Yamma, commended the troops for their courage and prompt response to the incidents.
The task force also reassured residents of Katsina, Zamfara and neighbouring states of its commitment to restoring lasting peace and security across the region.
